column3: Close to the Hebrew; “inciting you against us” is rendered “has set you against us.”
Close to the Hebrew; “in the mortar in the brick-terrace” is rendered “in the clay in the brick courtyard,” and “in the sight of the Jews” is moved forward.
Close to the Hebrew; “his state tent” is rendered “his royal pavilion.”

NKJV renders “he will delouse the land of Egypt as a shepherd delouses his garment” as “he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd puts on his garment”; the meaning of the verb is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “the gods of Egypt” is rendered “the gods of the Egyptians.”
